deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a library loan slip (Leihschein) or bibliographic request note, not a working sheet. It has four elements.

(1) Top, in brown ink, with 'Abhandlungen' underlined in red: the full title of a book, 'Abhandlungen, bei Begründung der Kön[iglich] sächsischen Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften herausgegeben von der Jablonowskischen Gesellschaft. Leipzig 1846.' This is the founding volume of the Royal Saxon Society of Sciences, published by the Fürstlich Jablonowskische Gesellschaft. Its best-known item is Wilhelm Weber's first memoir 'Elektrodynamische Maassbestimmungen' (1846). That memoir contains Weber's fundamental law of force between moving electric charges.

(2) Bottom right, in brown ink: the borrower's name 'Riemann', with a bracketed word below it. That word is most plausibly '(Weber)', naming the author or paper wanted, though the reading is uncertain.

(3) In grey pencil: a large cancellation stroke across the slip and a word at left. The word is probably 'zurück' or a similar return mark, showing the book was returned and the slip cancelled.

(4) In red pencil: a shelf or date mark read as 'Bl. 10. 58' or similar. If it is a date (e.g. '1. 10. 58' or 'Okt. 58'), it would fall in 1858. That is the year Riemann submitted 'Ein Beitrag zur Elektrodynamik' to the Göttingen Society and then withdrew it. That paper proposes that electric action propagates with finite speed, as an alternative grounding for Weber's law. A loan of Weber's 1846 memoir at that time would fit this context, but this is my inference and is not stated on the slip.

The archive foliation '34' is at right.

The neighbouring pages are a set of dance instructions (previous page) and an essentially blank, faint page (next page). This confirms that the 'Varia' bundle mixes non-mathematical papers.
